mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS declines for 3 months, or if the correlation between RSAFS changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and SPX returns is not significantly positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real income increases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL declines for 3 months, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL changes and SPX returns is not significantly positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business investment are likely to increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200,000, or if the correlation between PAYEMS changes and SPX returns is not significantly positive over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a robust demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase in the same month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase, or if the joint correlation between these series changes and SPX returns is not significantly positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly negative over a 3-year rolling window.
